title: Philly Steak and Cheese Sandwiches
subtitle: shaved seared steak, sweet soft onions and melty provolone piled into toasted garlic-butter rolls
imageAlt: Two toasted hoagie rolls filled with shaved steak, caramelized onions and melted provolone
servingsNote: 4 big sandwiches — dinner for two, plus 2 for lunch

beforeYouStart.text: Freeze the steak 30–40 minutes so you can shave it paper-thin.
Slice the steak as thin as you can, across the grain. No Frills sometimes sells 'fast-fry' or shaved steak — that works too.
Provolone is classic; mild white cheddar or mozzarella slices work too.

items.name: hoagie or sub rolls
items.note: split, not all the way through

steps.title: Soften the onions
steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp oil and the butter in a large skillet over medium. Add the onions with a pinch of salt and cook, stirring now and then, 12–15 minutes until soft and golden. Tip into a bowl.

steps.title: Toast the rolls
steps.text: Mix the softened butter with the garlic. Spread inside the rolls and toast cut side down in the hot pan (or under the broiler) 1–2 minutes until golden. Spread with mayo if using.

steps.title: Sear the steak
steps.text: Turn the heat to high and add the last 1 tbsp oil. Add the steak in a single layer (2 batches) and sear 1 minute without moving, then season with salt, pepper and garlic powder and chop/toss with a spatula 1–2 minutes until just cooked. Splash in the Worcestershire.

steps.title: Melt the cheese
steps.text: Return the onions and mix. Divide into 4 long piles in the pan, lay 2 slices of provolone over each and cover for 1 minute to melt.

steps.title: Fill and serve
steps.text: Slide a spatula under each pile and flip it into a toasted roll. Serve right away.

fixIt.fix: Slice thinner (partially frozen) and across the grain, and cook fast over high heat — overcooking makes it tough.
Pan was crowded or not hot enough. Cook in two batches.
Toast the roll well with the garlic butter first — it's a barrier.
Keep them at medium and add a splash of water if they colour too fast.

saleTip: Look for sirloin 'fast-fry' or value-pack steak on the No Frills flyer, and No Name provolone slices. Day-old sub rolls are fine once toasted.
swap: Chicken breast, sliced thin (cook to 74°C / 165°F) for chicken cheesesteaks. Swap provolone for Cheez Whiz-style sauce for the Philly-authentic version.
leftovers: Store the filling separately from the rolls, fridge 3 days.
doneness: Shaved steak cooks through in 2–3 minutes; steak is safe at 63°C (145°F)+.
source: Based on tested Philly cheesesteak methods (Serious Eats, Food Network Kitchen): partially frozen shaved steak, high-heat sear, cheese melted over the meat in the pan, toasted rolls.
gear: Large skillet or griddle with a lid
prepAhead: Cook the onions up to 3 days ahead.
Slice the steak a day ahead and keep covered in the fridge.
reheat: Reheat the filling in a skillet over medium 3–4 min until steaming, add fresh cheese to melt, and toast a fresh roll.

basic.note: Steak, onions and cheese in a toasted roll.

stepNotes.2: Basic: salt, pepper and garlic powder, no Worcestershire.

fancy.note: Caramelised onions, a creamy provolone sauce and garlic-butter toasted rolls.

stepNotes.0: Fancy: cook the onions 25 minutes on medium-low until deep golden.

addSteps.title: Fancy finish
addSteps.text: Melt 1 tbsp butter, stir in the flour, then whisk in the milk until thick. Off the heat, stir in the cheddar until smooth. Spoon the sauce into the rolls before the steak and provolone.

plating: Wrap the bottom half of each sandwich in parchment — deli style.
Let a little cheese sauce drip over the edge.

why.0-2: Slow-softened onions add sweetness. Skip them and it's just steak and cheese.
why.1-1: Buttered, toasted rolls stay crisp under the juicy filling.

funFact: The Philly cheesesteak began in 1930 at Pat Olivieri’s hot dog stand in Philadelphia, as a grilled beef sandwich. The cheese was added years later.
